newsitem.title: USA: Teen killer indicted, toughter laws called for.
newsitem.headline: Teen killer indicted, toughter laws called for.

text.p: Brooklyn District Attorney Charles Hynes Friday called for tougher laws against juvenile offenders after announcing a 10-count indictment against a 14-year-old boy accused of a cold-blooded killing.

Hynes told a news conference John Hale, 14, of Brooklyn had been charged with murder, attempted murder, assault and weapons possession stemming from the May 27 murder of Latasha Flowers, 21, also of Brooklyn.
She was shot while walking with her fiance and her brother, 17-year-old Calvin Flowers, who was shot in the foot.

Det. Tom Ferro, who arrested Hale, said the teen was with about five other youths when Flowers walked by. One of them apparently did not like the look she gave them and told Hale: "Shoot 'em." He allegedly pulled out a semi-automatic handgun and shot Flowers in the chest, then shot her brother.
"This is a shocking example of wanton and senseless violence. The sheer brutality of this crime underscores the inadequacy of the juvenile justice laws in this state," Hynes said.

"We need to treat adult-level violence with adult-level punishment," he said. "It is time to send an unmistakable message to violent teenagers that the taking of life is a gravely serious act that will be punished by a very long period of incarceration."

If convicted as a youth Hale faces a minimum sentence of five years in jail and a maximum sentence of nine years to life. As an adult he faces a minimum sentence of 15 years and a maximum of 25 years to life.
